Dataset and evaluation
Normal versus pneumonia on the Kermany pediatric benchmark
Historical baseline: 5,232 training records and 624 test records
New split: 4,164 training, 1,042 validation and 624 test records
The benchmark test was inspected previously. It is not an external blind holdout.
The verified M2 baseline
Five pretrained CNNs, five epochs, majority voting. Paper target: 96.4% accuracy.
Accuracy 92.15% · pneumonia recall 94.62% · specificity 88.03%
Macro F1 0.916 · ROC AUC 0.962
28 false positives, 21 false negatives. ResNet18 alone: 93.11% accuracy.
Why focus on the lungs?
The full image includes peripheral anatomy and acquisition markings
A fixed pretrained anatomical model predicts both lungs at 256 pixels
We crop their union with a 10% margin, then resize for classification
256 replaces the standard 512 input for CPU runtime. Failed masks fall back.
Median retained crop area: 71.1% of original image area

The implementation and its limits
Frozen pretrained image encoders with five-epoch trained classifier heads
ResNet18 supplies CNN features. DeiT-Tiny supplies transformer features.
The pilot isolates image region and classifier combination under one split
This reduced experiment differs from the original five-CNN late-block proposal.

Conclusions and remaining questions
Predeclared crop CNN–ViT: 93.75% accuracy and 98.21% pneumonia recall
Small pediatric data and imperfect identifier groups limit generalization
Adding ViT to the crop CNN improved accuracy by 1.12 percentage points
The validation/test reversal requires repeated splits and external testing.
